sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc-Lko:34892
Court No. - 27

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 13173 of 2022
Applicant :- Pradeep Rawat
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Jitendra Pratap Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rajesh Kumar Singh, learned A.G.A.-I for the State.
2. In compliance of earlier order, the prosecutrix has been brought by Sub-Inspector Sri Alok Kumar Yadav and Lady Constable Ms. Rekha.
3. This bail application has been filed by the applicant with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No.44 of 2022 under Section 323/354/504/506/376/406 IPC, PS Sairpur district Lucknow.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has invited attention of this Court towards the statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 CrPC in which the prosecutrix has stated that in 2018, she met with the applicant and thereafter, they used to talk together and on the pretext of marriage, physical relation was made between them.
She stated that many times physical relation was made by applicant.
It has been submitted that it is a case of consent and age of the girl is 23 years and she is major.
He has submitted that prosecutrix performed marriage in Arya Samaj Mandir on 18.1.2020 Pradeep Rawat vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

1 with one Ramesh and due to that reason, the relation with the applicant became bitter.
He has stated that it is the prosecutrix who cheated the applicant and not the applicant.
The medical report has not supported the prosecution case
He has further submitted that since the prosecutrix is already married woman, how can the applicant marry her.

He has submitted that the applicant has no criminal history and he is in Jail since 12.5.2022.
5.
On the other hand, learned AGA has opposed the bail and has submitted that it is a case of rape and against her will rape was committed, therefore, bail application is liable to be rejected.

6. Considering the over all facts and circumstances of the case, the statement under Section 164 CrPC, the argument of consent and other argument that the prosecutrix is already married with one Ramesh, it is a fit case for bail.
7. Let the applicant Pradeep Rawat be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

8. It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The Trial Court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything in this order.
